<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/data/:object (route, 64 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4a16d887b3f89b64ca36815bed56c3fea12dc1be` — the merge of head `901010d4d8a577742867e4f6384c7e231746e76b` into base `33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4a16d887b3f89b64ca36815bed56c3fea12dc1be && git checkout 4a16d887b3f89b64ca36815bed56c3fea12dc1be
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4 901010d4d8a577742867e4f6384c7e231746e76b && git checkout -B drift-repro 33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4 && git merge --no-ff 901010d4d8a577742867e4f6384c7e231746e76b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33b6e8bece79e70156dc2c1880813f8d88af61d4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `901010d4d8a577742867e4f6384c7e231746e76b`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20701 body and all ten comments (governing: `5897601448`, `5906762084`, `5909519064`, `5910777625`, `5914220480`, `5916019187`); #20805 and PR #20834 (merged as `b28054654`, an ancestor of the merge-base); PR #20905 body, file list (4 files) and the net diff `4edb61449b...901010d4d8` (265 insertions, 9 deletions); the check-runs on the head, polled to convergence. Source premises were read on the merge-base `4edb61449b` by `git show`; nothing was built, run or checked out.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) `toFailedResult` reads `field` off the envelope — right, and within item 2.**
- Same field as the create door, on both halves. The engine's declared-field door stamps `err.field = undeclared[0]` and `err.fields = undeclared` (bare strings) (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:1844-1870`). The door's `structuredCodeAnswer` INVALID_FIELD arm ships that same `error.field` (`packages/rest/src/error-response.ts:1261-1272`), and `classifyDataError` consults the structured arms before anything else (`:1295-1296`). On the dry run, `ObjectQL.validate` throws the same envelope from the same function (`engine.ts:12251-12256`), it propagates out of `previewVerdict` (`import-runner.ts:534-541`) into the row's catch and `toFailedResult` (`:878-881`). On the commit, the bulk path carries the door's per-row envelope as `outcomes[i].error` (`engine.ts:12852`, `:13408-13410`; `protocol.ts:13579-13598` passes outcomes through) into `toFailedResult(rowNo, res.error)` (`import-runner.ts:765`); the upsert update path throws through `updateData` into the same catch. Both halves submit the same `coerceRow` payload — the bulk flush adds only `id` (`:641`), a platform-provisioned key the door tolerates — so `undeclared[0]` is identical on dry run, commit and door. Pinned by the row-versus-door case in `import-row-report-field-20701.test.ts`.
- Unique conflict: true. `DuplicateRecordError` carries `field` from `uniqueViolationColumn` (`packages/objectql/src/duplicate-record-error.ts:79-101`, index names refused), and the 409 arm reads `field` off that envelope ("the envelope is the contract", `error-response.ts:1085-1088`). The row's `error` sentence already named the column in prose (`sanitizeRowError`, `import-runner.ts:285-288`); the structured key now matches. Item 2 as written (`5906762084`, restated in `5910777625`) is "names the field from the error envelope's `field` member", with no code qualifier, so this is inside item 2, not beyond it.
- Non-column `field`: none found. Every `field`-stamping producer reachable from the runner names a field: the write door (`engine.ts:1866`), the read doors the upsert match lookup can reach through `findData` (`engine.ts:1719`; `protocol.ts:9969, 10077, 10152, 10232, 10712, 10920, 11023, 11176`, each `err.field = first` unknown or unmaterializable field name), the duplicate envelope. `ValidationError` carries `fields[]` only (`record-validator.ts:226-243`), so a finding keeps priority; raw driver errors carry no `field`. The new guard (`head !== null && typeof head === 'object'`) stops a string entry of `fields` being read as a finding, which the base code did not guard against (it merely got `undefined`).

**(b) The driver-string branch — right; code, status, field, object verified unchanged.** The body literal's `status: 400`, `code: 'INVALID_FIELD'`, `...(field ? { field } : {})`, `...(object ? { object } : {})` are untouched in the diff (`error-response.ts:1795-1805`); only the two `error` strings move. The new sentence is truthful: it states what the driver said (the table has no such column) and conditions the drift diagnosis on "If the object declares", which is the one case the door "by construction cannot see" (`engine.ts:1806-1810`). Exposure: nothing new — `object` was already in the old sentence ("on object 'X'"), `field` is the same regex capture, and the raw driver text is not interpolated. `os migrate` is a real command (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/`) and the sibling not-null branch already prescribes it (`:1820-1822`). An undeclared key is answered exactly as before wherever the door has an opinion: the engine refuses it before any driver and its message "Unknown field 'nope' on object 'proj_20701'" ships verbatim through the structured arm; pinned by the control case. Two residues, neither wrong and neither a verdict mover: (i) the no-capture fallback sentence inside the same branch also changed (reachable only when the capture ends in a dot) and neither the PR body nor the changeset mentions it; (ii) on a registry-less host where the door has no opinion (`engine.ts:1817-1835`) an undeclared key reaches the driver and now gets the conditional sentence rather than "Unknown field", with code, status, field and object unchanged — the PR's "untouched" claim is about the engine's sentence and is true. No hand-written doc quotes the branch's old sentence; `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx:536` shows the engine door's wording, still true.

**(c) Item 1 not delivered — each premise holds on the merge-base.**
- Premise 1 HOLDS: `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.validateData` forwards `mode` and `context` only, no listener (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:11793-11799`), while `ObjectQL.validate` reports drops only through its `onFieldsDropped` option (`engine.ts:12194-12208`, `:12346-12358`).
- Premise 2 HOLDS: `ValidateDataResponseSchema` declares `object`, `mode`, `valid`, `results`, `posture` and nothing else (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:2122-2148`); `validate` returns that type, so the engine's own return carries no drop either.
- Premise 3 HOLDS: `insertManyData` collects every event into one listener and returns `mergeDroppedFieldEvents(dropped)` at batch level (`protocol.ts:13577-13598`, merge at `:2277-2310`); its docblock says "Read a name here as AT LEAST ONE row dropped this field, never this row dropped it" and "Restoring row precision means giving the engine's drop report a per-row channel ... never a reconstruction at this call site" (`:13517-13564`); `ObjectQL.insertMany`'s docblock says the same (`engine.ts:13470-13483`). The runner takes this path whenever the protocol offers `insertManyData` (`import-runner.ts:577`, `:663`), which the real protocol does. Nuance the PR states correctly: the non-bulk seams (`createData` `protocol.ts:11831-11836`, `updateData`) report per call and the runner discards it today (`:847`, `:871`), but item 1 says "dry run and commit alike" and the dry run has no channel at all, so the item is undeliverable inside `packages/rest`.
- Options as written: A names objectql (`InsertManyRowOutcome` is objectql's own type, `engine.ts:190`, so a per-outcome drop is one package), spec (`ValidateDataResponseSchema`, `ImportRowResultSchema` — `ImportJobResultsSchema` at `export.zod.ts:429` reuses the row schema, so the async sample follows), metadata-protocol (`validateData` forwarding, per-outcome `droppedFields` on `insertManyData`) and rest: complete. One accuracy nuance: "the async job persists it through its existing results JSON" — `sys_import_job.results` is a CAPPED sample, failures first (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-import-job.object.ts:71-74`), so a drop on an ok row survives the async path only inside the sample; A does not say so. B names spec (`ValidateDataResponseSchema`, `ImportResponseSchema`, `ImportJobResultsSchema`), metadata-protocol (`validateData`), platform-objects (`sys_import_job` column plus generated bundles) and rest (sync route `rest-server.ts:9122`, job worker `:9286`, results route): complete and accurate. Neither owes a `packages/client` edit (typed from spec); both leave objectui unmeasured; spec artifact regeneration is routine, not a layer. No choice between A and B is made here.

**(d) Changeset (`@objectstack/rest` patch): accurate, and it claims nothing undelivered.** Title follows the existing `(#N)` convention. Paragraph 1 (INVALID_FIELD rows carry `field` on dry run and commit; a finding still wins; a unique conflict row names its column "when the database said which column it was, as the 409 does") and paragraph 2 (the drift sentence; "code, status, field and object are unchanged") are each pinned or verified above. The drop signal is not mentioned. Omission only, not a false claim: the fallback-sentence change in (b)(i).

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no` with `patch` is right. `field` is an existing optional key of `ImportRowResultSchema` (`packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts:328`, `z.string().optional()`), now filled in more cases; no key is added, no accept set moves, and the 400 body's free-text `error` is not a keyed surface; no code is minted. The claim's `yes (widening)` (`5914220480`) presupposed the drop-signal key, which is not in this diff, and the claim itself told the dev to re-read against the real diff. AGENTS.md: a bug fix in a released package takes `patch`. `check-widening-tells` NOT MEASURED (no declared surface covers the four files) is consistent with that reading.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `deviations`, each answered:
1. `Part of #20701`, not a closing keyword — right; item 1 is undelivered and the card must stay open; `Part-of PR must not also close its card` is green.
2. `Clause-②: no` — answered in ②.
3. Stop line held — the file list is three paths under `packages/rest/src` plus one `.changeset`; the net diff against the merge-base confirms it; no governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success).
4. `origin/main` merged before opening — the net diff is the four files; fine.
5. vitest bare `--` trap, own recorded process group stopped, nothing cited — within multi-agent §8 (a recorded pid); accepted.
6. Container restart, everything re-run on the head — accepted; CI on the head is the gate.
7. `check:query-options-erasure` red then fixed by typing the options — `Lint & Repo Gates` success on the head.
8. Pre-push refusal on a `Part of` commit line, unpublished commit amended — accepted; `ceadff28fd`, `8872905c9f`, `901010d4d8` carry the model-free trailer pair; the merge commit `6eb88d7028` carries none, which the queue's squash makes moot.
9. Attribution — the PR body ends with the session-URL footer; no model identifier in title, body, commits or changeset. Accepted.
10. `label-write` for the PR assignee only — mirrors the card's assignee; accepted.
11. Two throwaway probe files created and deleted uncommitted — not in the file list; accepted.
12. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally — `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger` and `Build Core` are success on the head; accepted.

Dev `out_of_scope_findings`:
1. **Schema-drift row (declared field, no column, import commit answers the driver's `SQLITE_ERROR` text) — ESCALATED to the dispatching seat.** Triage's `5897601448` does NOT already cover it: that sentence is scoped to "a column the check can judge", and a declared field whose column is missing is exactly what the declared-field door "by construction cannot see" (`engine.ts:1806-1810`); the split `5906762084` fixed the REST half at three items, none of which is this, and the maintainer's 「20701 同意」 confirmed that scope with "nothing about its scope changes". Class (a) is right (reproducible, probe named, the pin file's docblock records the drift cell). Reach is right but understated: the same `runImport` serves the async job (`rest-server.ts:9122` and `:9286`), so job row results carry the same text; measured on SQLite only, and Postgres or MySQL arrive with their own dialect text, unmeasured. The dev's "fold it into the remaining half" follows the os-dev playbook's same-family rule (name the family's closing card, no single-point card), but the fold itself is a scope change on a maintainer-confirmed split and is triage's call, not the dev's or this record's. Not a verdict mover: the finding is outside this diff.
2. **`ImportRowResult.warnings` undeclared on the spec's `ImportRowResultSchema` — carrier conditionally right; ESCALATED.** The finding is accurate: the runner emits `warnings` on dry-run ok rows (`import-runner.ts:838`), `ImportRowResultSchema` declares no such key (`export.zod.ts:322-331`) and `ImportJobResultsSchema` reuses it (`:429`). The named carrier (the drop-signal PR) will edit `packages/spec/src/api/export.zod.ts` under either option, so it is "the PR that will touch that file"; but under B the row schema is otherwise untouched and declaring `warnings` there becomes a rider, and a carrier binds only if that child's claim names it. It is a contract-first (spec lane) served-but-undeclared key; "no consumer measured" makes it un-exercised drift, which the playbook keeps off the board. The seat should write it into the drop-signal child's claim as a declared surface (spec plus rest), or file it `domain:spec` if that child is scoped B.

Check-runs on `901010d4d8` (converged 2026-09-30T17:15:40Z; 34 runs, collapsed to latest-per-name): 31 `success`, 3 `skipped` (`Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failure, 0 in progress. The seven required contexts are all `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (rollup and shards 1-6), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (rollup and 1-3), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. No governed surface is in the file list; the PR is a draft, per the dispatch.
